title: The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
place: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania
description: Melvyn Bragg and guests on the vast union of Poland and Lithuania, formalized in 1569, which elected its kings and lasted until it was carved up in the 1790s. The grand dukes’ palace, torn down in 1801, was rebuilt in 2018.
spotify: In Our Time The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
apple: In Our Time The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth

title: Europe’s last pagans
description: Historians Eleanor Janega and Francis Young on Lithuania, the last pagan state in Europe, and its conversion to Christianity in 1387. The cathedral is said to stand on the site of a temple to the thunder god Perkūnas.

title: The Gaon of Vilna
show: The Jewish History Podcast - With Rabbi Yaakov Wolbe
episode: Ep. 34: Great Jewish Personalities: The Gaon of Vilna
description: On Rabbi Elijah ben Solomon, the Vilna Gaon, the great 18th-century scholar who made Vilna a center of Jewish learning, known as the Jerusalem of the North. His bust stands on Jews’ Street, near where the Great Synagogue stood.

title: The Paper Brigade
episode: [On the Holocaust]  The Vilna Ghetto “Paper Brigade”
description: On the poets Shmerke Kaczerginski and Abraham Sutzkever, forced by the Nazis to sort Jewish books and documents for destruction, who smuggled thousands of them into hiding in the Vilna ghetto instead.

title: The book smugglers
episode: Lithuanian Book Smugglers Vs. The Russian Empire
description: From 1864 to 1904 the Russian Empire banned Lithuanian books in the Latin alphabet. Smugglers carried them across the border from Prussia by the millions. The national library is named after the author of the first Lithuanian book.
spotify: Ridiculous History Lithuanian Book Smugglers Vs. The Russian Empire
apple: Ridiculous History Lithuanian Book Smugglers Vs. The Russian Empire

title: The Lithuanian language
description: Historian Francis Young on Lithuanian, a language that kept so many ancient features that linguists study it to reconstruct the parent of most European languages. Vilnius University was founded in 1579.
spotify: A Language I Love Is... Lithuanian and Francis Young
apple: A Language I Love Is... Lithuanian and Francis Young

title: January 13, 1991
description: A protester remembers the night of January 13, 1991, when Soviet troops and tanks seized the TV tower, ten months after Lithuania declared independence. Fourteen unarmed civilians were killed.
